**USS _North Carolina_**, [hull number](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_number "Hull number")**BB-55**, is the [lead ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lead_ship "Lead ship") of the [_North Carolina_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina-class_battleship "North Carolina-class battleship") of [fast battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_battleship "Fast battleship"), the first vessel of the type built for the [United States Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy "United States Navy"). Built under the [Washington Treaty system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Naval_Treaty "Washington Naval Treaty"), _North Carolina_'s design was [limited in displacement and armament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_battleship "Treaty battleship"), though the United States used a clause in the [Second London Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_London_Naval_Treaty "Second London Naval Treaty") to increase the main battery from the original armament of twelve 14-inch (356 mm) guns in quadruple turrets to nine 16 in (406 mm) guns in triple turrets. The ship was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") in 1937 and completed in April 1941, while the United States was still neutral during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").

Following the Japanese [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") in December, _North Carolina_ mobilized for war and was initially sent to counter a possible sortie by the German battleship [_Tirpitz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Tirpitz "German battleship Tirpitz"), though this did not materialize and _North Carolina_ was promptly transferred to the Pacific to strengthen Allied forces during the [Guadalcanal campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalcanal_campaign "Guadalcanal campaign"). There, she screened [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier") engaged in the campaign and took part in the [Battle of the Eastern Solomons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Eastern_Solomons "Battle of the Eastern Solomons") on 24–25 August 1942, where she shot down several Japanese aircraft. The next month, she was [torpedoed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torpedo "Torpedo") by a Japanese [submarine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine "Submarine") but was not seriously damaged. After repairs, she returned to the campaign and continued to screen carriers during the campaigns across the central Pacific in 1943 and 1944, including the [Gilberts and Marshall Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_and_Marshall_Islands_campaign "Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign") and the [Mariana and Palau Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_and_Palau_Islands_campaign "Mariana and Palau Islands campaign"), where she saw action during the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea "Battle of the Philippine Sea").

The ship was undergoing a refit during the invasion of the Philippines but took part in the later stages of the [Philippines campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_campaign_(1944%E2%80%931945) "Philippines campaign (1944–1945)") and was present when the fleet was damaged by [Typhoon Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Cobra "Typhoon Cobra"). She took part in offensive operations in support of the [Battles of Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Iwo_Jima "Battle of Iwo Jima") and [Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Okinawa "Battle of Okinawa") in 1945, including numerous attacks on Japan. Following the [surrender of Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrender_of_Japan "Surrender of Japan") in August, she carried American personnel home during [Operation Magic Carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Magic_Carpet "Operation Magic Carpet"). _North Carolina_ operated briefly off the east coast of the United States in 1946 before being [decommissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning "Ship commissioning") the next year and placed in reserve. Stricken from the [Naval Vessel Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Vessel_Register "Naval Vessel Register") in 1960, the ship was saved from the [breaker's yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_breaking "Ship breaking") by a campaign to preserve the vessel as a [museum ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_ship "Museum ship") in her namesake state. In 1962, the _North Carolina_ museum was opened in [Wilmington, North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_North_Carolina "Wilmington, North Carolina").

## Design

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Design")]

Main article: [_North Carolina_-class battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina-class_battleship "North Carolina-class battleship")

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7e/North_Carolina_class_battleship_recognition_drawings.jpg/250px-North_Carolina_class_battleship_recognition_drawings.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:North_Carolina_class_battleship_recognition_drawings.jpg)

Recognition drawing of the _North Carolina_ class

The _North Carolina_ class was the first new battleship design built under the [Washington Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Naval_Treaty "Washington Naval Treaty") system; her design was bound by the terms of the [Second London Naval Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_London_Naval_Treaty "Second London Naval Treaty") of 1936, which added a restriction on her [main battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Main_battery "Main battery") of guns that they be no larger than 14 inches (356 mm). The [General Board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Board_of_the_United_States_Navy "General Board of the United States Navy") evaluated a number of designs ranging from traditional 23-knot (43 km/h; 26 mph) battleships akin to the ["standard" series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard-type_battleship "Standard-type battleship") or [fast battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_battleship "Fast battleship"), and ultimately a fast battleship armed with twelve 14-inch guns was selected. After the ships were authorized, however, the United States invoked the escalator clause in the treaty that permitted an increase to 16 in (406 mm) guns in the event that any member nation refused to sign the treaty, which Japan refused to do.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985244%E2%80%93265-2)

_North Carolina_ is 728 feet 9 inches (222.12 m)[long overall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Length_overall "Length overall") and has a [beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beam_(nautical) "Beam (nautical)") of 108 ft 4 in (33.02 m) and a [draft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draft_(hull) "Draft (hull)") of 32 ft 11.5 in (10.046 m). Her [standard displacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_displacement "Standard displacement") amounted to 35,000 [long tons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_ton "Long ton") (35,562[t](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tonne "Tonne")) and increased to 44,800 long tons (45,519 t) at [full combat load](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full-load_displacement "Full-load displacement"). The ship was powered by four [General Electric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric "General Electric")[steam turbines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_turbines "Steam turbines"), each driving one propeller shaft, using steam provided by eight oil-fired [Babcock & Wilcox boilers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babcock_&_Wilcox_boiler "Babcock & Wilcox boiler"). Rated at 121,000 [shaft horsepower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horsepower#Shaft_horsepower "Horsepower") (90,000[kW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilowatt "Kilowatt")), the turbines were intended to give a top speed of 28 [knots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)") (52 km/h; 32 mph). The ship had a cruising range of 17,450 [nautical miles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautical_mile "Nautical mile") (32,320 km; 20,080 mi) at a speed of 15 knots (28 km/h; 17 mph). She carried three [Vought OS2U Kingfisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vought_OS2U_Kingfisher "Vought OS2U Kingfisher")[floatplanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floatplane "Floatplane") for aerial reconnaissance, which were launched by a pair of [aircraft catapults](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_catapult "Aircraft catapult") on her [fantail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantail_(ship) "Fantail (ship)"). Her peace time crew numbered 1,800 officers and enlisted men, but during the war the crew swelled to 99 officers and 2,035 enlisted.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_198097-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985447-4)

The ship is armed with a main battery of nine [16 in /45 caliber Mark 6 guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/16%22/45_caliber_Mark_6_gun "16\"/45 caliber Mark 6 gun")[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-5) in a trio of three-[gun turrets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gun_turret "Gun turret") on the centerline, two of which were placed in a [superfiring pair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfire "Superfire") forward, with the third aft. The [secondary battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_armament "Secondary armament") consisted of twenty [5 in (127 mm) /38 caliber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5%22/38_caliber_gun "5\"/38 caliber gun")[dual-purpose guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual-purpose_gun "Dual-purpose gun") mounted in twin turrets clustered [amidships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amidships "Amidships"), five turrets on either side. As designed, the ship was equipped with an anti-aircraft battery of sixteen [1.1 in (28 mm) /75-caliber guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1.1-inch/75-caliber_gun "1.1-inch/75-caliber gun") and eighteen .50-caliber (12.7 mm) [M2 Browning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M2_Browning "M2 Browning") machine guns,[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-6) but her anti-aircraft battery was expanded greatly during her career.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_198097-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985447-4)

The main [armored belt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armored_belt "Armored belt") is 12 in (305 mm) thick, while the main armored deck is up to 5.5 in (140 mm) thick. The main battery gun turrets have 16 in (406 mm) thick faces, and they were mounted atop [barbettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbette "Barbette") that were protected with the same thickness of steel. The [conning tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conning_tower "Conning tower") had 14.7 in (373 mm) thick sides. The ship's armor layout was designed with opponents equipped with 14-inch guns in mind, but since the treaty system broke down just before construction began, her design could not be revised to improve the scale of protection to defend against heavier guns. Despite this shortcoming, the _North Carolina_ class proved to be more successful battleships than the better-armored but very cramped [_South Dakota_ class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dakota-class_battleship_(1939) "South Dakota-class battleship (1939)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_198097-3)

### Modifications

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Modifications")]

_North Carolina_ received a number of upgrades over the course of her career, primarily consisting of radar and improved anti-aircraft batteries. By November 1942, the ship had received three Mark 3 [fire-control radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fire-control_radar "Fire-control radar") sets for the main battery, four Mark 4 radars for the secondary guns, a [CXAM air-search radar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CXAM_radar "CXAM radar"), and an [SG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SG_radar "SG radar")surface-search radar. During her early 1944 refit, she received an [SK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_radar "SK radar")air-search radar in place of the CXAM and a second SG radar; her Mark 3 radars were replaced with more advanced Mark 8 sets, though she retained one of the Mark 3s as a backup. In September, the SK radar was replaced with an SK-2 set, and her Mark 4 radars were replaced with a combination of Mark 12 and Mark 22 sets. After the war, she received a secondary SR air search radar and an SCR-720 search radar.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985276-7)

During her refit in late 1942, _North Carolina_'s anti-aircraft battery was replaced with ten quadruple-mount [40 mm (1.6 in) Bofors guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bofors_40_mm_Automatic_Gun_L/60 "Bofors 40 mm Automatic Gun L/60") (forty guns), and forty-six [20 mm (0.79 in) Oerlikon autocannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oerlikon_20_mm_cannon#World_War_II "Oerlikon 20 mm cannon") in single mounts. By June 1943, her anti-aircraft armament had been increased with four more 40 mm quadruple mounts, and in November, an additional mount was added atop the rear main battery turret, giving her 60 Bofors guns in 15 quad mounts. Two more 20 mm cannon were added by late 1944, and another eight were installed in April 1945. By the end of the war in August, her 20 mm battery had been reduced to eight twin mounts and twenty single mounts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985276%E2%80%93277-8)

## Service history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Service history")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/USS_North_Carolina_Fit_out_NARA_1941-04-17.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_Fit_out_NARA_1941-04-17.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_Fit_out_NARA_1941-04-17.jpg)

[Fitting-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fitting-out "Fitting-out") stage, 17 April 1941

The [keel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel "Keel") for _North Carolina_ was [laid down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keel_laying "Keel laying") at the [New York Naval Shipyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_Naval_Shipyard "New York Naval Shipyard") on 27 October 1937. Her completed [hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hull_(watercraft) "Hull (watercraft)") was [launched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceremonial_ship_launching "Ceremonial ship launching") on 13 June 1940 and the ship was [commissioned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_commissioning "Ship commissioning") into the fleet on 9 April 1941[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) in a ceremony attended by [Governor of North Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_North_Carolina "Governor of North Carolina")[J. Melville Broughton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Melville_Broughton "J. Melville Broughton").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-10) The ship's first commanding officer was Captain [Olaf M. Hustvedt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olaf_M._Hustvedt "Olaf M. Hustvedt"). _North Carolina_ embarked on her [shakedown cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakedown_cruise "Shakedown cruise") in the [Caribbean Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea") and spent the rest of the year working up while the United States remained neutral during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"). Following the Japanese [attack on Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attack_on_Pearl_Harbor "Attack on Pearl Harbor") on 7 December, _North Carolina_ began extensive battle training to prepare for combat in the [Pacific War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_War "Pacific War").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)

Her first operation came in April 1942, when she was deployed to [Naval Station Argentia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Station_Argentia "Naval Station Argentia") on 23 April as part of a force intended to block a potential sortie by the German battleship [_Tirpitz_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_battleship_Tirpitz "German battleship Tirpitz") if she attempted to break out into the [convoy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Convoy "Convoy") lanes of the North Atlantic. _Tirpitz_ remained in Norway, however, and _North Carolina_ was quickly replaced by the battleship [_South Dakota_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_South_Dakota_(BB-57) "USS South Dakota (BB-57)"), allowing _North Carolina_ to get underway for the Pacific in mid-1942. She passed through the [Panama Canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal "Panama Canal") on 10 June in company with the [aircraft carriers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aircraft_carrier "Aircraft carrier")[_Wasp_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Wasp_(CV-7) "USS Wasp (CV-7)") and [_Long Island_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Long_Island_(CVE-1) "USS Long Island (CVE-1)") and nine [destroyers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destroyer "Destroyer"). On 15 June, _North Carolina_ was assigned to Task Force (TF) 18, centered on _Wasp_, along with four cruisers and nine destroyers, under the command of [Rear Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rear_Admiral "Rear Admiral")[Leigh Noyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leigh_Noyes "Leigh Noyes").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer160,_172-11)

### Guadalcanal campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Guadalcanal campaign")]

Main article: [Guadalcanal campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalcanal_campaign "Guadalcanal campaign")

_North Carolina_ was sent to join the Guadalcanal campaign as part of [TF 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Task_Force_16 "Task Force 16"), which also included the aircraft carrier [_Enterprise_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Enterprise_(CV-6) "USS Enterprise (CV-6)"), the [heavy cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_cruiser "Heavy cruiser")[_Portland_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Portland_(CA-33) "USS Portland (CA-33)"), the [light cruiser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_cruiser "Light cruiser")[_Atlanta_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Atlanta_(CL-51) "USS Atlanta (CL-51)"), and six destroyers.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank173-12) The unit was part of [TF 61](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Task_Force_61 "Task Force 61"), commanded by [Vice Admiral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_Admiral "Vice Admiral")[Frank Fletcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Jack_Fletcher "Frank Jack Fletcher"), and sent to cover the landing of the [1st Marine Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Marine_Division_(United_States) "1st Marine Division (United States)") on [Guadalcanal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalcanal "Guadalcanal") to seize the airfield being constructed there by the Japanese. TF 61 also included the carriers [_Saratoga_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Saratoga_(CV-3) "USS Saratoga (CV-3)") and _Wasp_. _North Carolina_ covered _Enterprise_ on the first day of the invasion of Guadalcanal and [Tulagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tulagi "Tulagi") on 7 August, and thereafter remained in company with _Enterprise_ to protect the carrier from Japanese air attacks. Fear of Japanese land-based torpedo bombers prompted Fletcher to withdraw the carrier groups the next day. The initial landing met little resistance, but a Japanese cruiser squadron attacked the invasion fleet on the night of 9 August, inflicting a major defeat on Allied naval forces in the [Battle of Savo Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Savo_Island "Battle of Savo Island").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer183,_185%E2%80%93186-13) The Navy briefly considered forming a surface combat force to counter the Japanese cruisers that would have been centered on _North Carolina_, with five heavy and one light cruiser and four destroyers, but it was determined that the need to protect the carrier task forces was too great to strip away their heavy units.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHornfischer123-14)

In this role, she participated in the [Battle of the Eastern Solomons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Eastern_Solomons "Battle of the Eastern Solomons") on 24–25 August. American forces had detected a group of Japanese carriers on the 24th and immediately launched attacks from _Saratoga_ that sank the [light carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_carrier "Light carrier")[_Ryūjō_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Ry%C5%ABj%C5%8D "Japanese aircraft carrier Ryūjō"). A Japanese counterattack struck the American fleet, and _North Carolina_ was the first to detect it, shortly after 16:00, using her air-search radar.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHornfischer115-15) The Japanese initially concentrated on _Enterprise_, and _North Carolina_ contributed her anti-aircraft fire to her defense. _Enterprise_ increased speed to 30 knots (56 km/h; 35 mph), causing _North Carolina_ to drop back, ultimately falling to around 4,000 yards (3,700 m) astern. A group of seven [Aichi D3A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aichi_D3A "Aichi D3A")[dive bombers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dive_bomber "Dive bomber") attacked _North Carolina_ at 16:43 but they all missed. _North Carolina_ emerged from the battle unscathed, though one man was killed by a [strafing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strafing "Strafing") aircraft. _Enterprise_ was hit by three bombs but aircraft from _Saratoga_ severely damaged the [seaplane tender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seaplane_tender "Seaplane tender")[_Chitose_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_aircraft_carrier_Chitose "Japanese aircraft carrier Chitose") in return.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank174%E2%80%93184-16)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_2014233%E2%80%93234-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer191-18)

_North Carolina_'s anti-aircraft claimed to have shot down between 7 and 14 aircraft,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) though evaluation of the gunners' effectiveness is mixed. The historian [Richard B. Frank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_B._Frank "Richard B. Frank") noted that the Japanese lost a total of eighteen D3As and credited _Enterprise_'s [Grumman F4F Wildcat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grumman_F4F_Wildcat "Grumman F4F Wildcat")[fighters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter_aircraft "Fighter aircraft") with half of them, with the rest shot down by the ships, "with the lion's share to gunners aboard _Enterprise_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank184-19) The naval analyst [Norman Friedman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Friedman "Norman Friedman") highlighted the effectiveness of the 5-inch guns aboard _Enterprise_ and _North Carolina_, but noted that the ship had difficulty tracking targets with her fire control radar, owing to a combination of rapid maneuvering to avoid attacks, excessive vibration from steaming at high speed, and the number of friendly and hostile aircraft aloft. Contemporary observers took an optimistic view of the ship's performance; her captain credited her with shooting down five to seven aircraft, Admiral [Chester W. Nimitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_W._Nimitz "Chester W. Nimitz"), the [Commander, U.S. Pacific Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commander,_U.S._Pacific_Fleet "Commander, U.S. Pacific Fleet"), noted that her 5-inch fire was particularly effective in dissuading Japanese attacks.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_2014233%E2%80%93245-20)

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/USS_North_Carolina_front_starboard_view_NARA_19LCM-BB55-4899-42.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_front_starboard_view_NARA_19LCM-BB55-4899-42.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_front_starboard_view_NARA_19LCM-BB55-4899-42.jpg)

_North Carolina_ in Pearl Harbor in November 1942 for repairs

While _Enterprise_ withdrew for repairs, _North Carolina_ was transferred to [TF 17](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Task_Force_17 "Task Force 17") to cover _Saratoga_, along with _Atlanta_ and a pair of destroyers.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHornfischer118-21) The ships operated off Guadalcanal for the next several weeks, during which time Japanese [submarines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine "Submarine") attempted to torpedo _North Carolina_ twice. The first, on 6 September, passed some 300 yd (270 m) off her [port](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_and_starboard "Port and starboard") side, but the second, from the submarine [_I-19_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_submarine_I-19 "Japanese submarine I-19") on 15 September, damaged the ship. _I-19_ had fired a spread of six torpedoes at _Wasp_ in TF 18, two or three of which hit. Two of the [Type 95 torpedoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_95_torpedo "Type 95 torpedo") continued on to the ships of TF 17, some 5 nautical miles (9.3 km; 5.8 mi) away. One hit the destroyer [_O'Brien_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_O'Brien_(DD-415) "USS O'Brien (DD-415)"), and a fourth hit _North Carolina_. The hit on _North Carolina_ struck the ship 20 ft (6.1 m) below the [waterline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterline "Waterline") on her port side and tore a 32-by-18-foot (9.8 by 5.5 m) hole in the plating. Five men were killed in the attack, but the torpedo inflicted little serious damage, apart from the shock of the blast that disabled the forward turret. Flooding occurred and _North Carolina_ took on a [list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angle_of_list "Angle of list") of 5.5 degrees to port, but this was quickly corrected with counter-flooding and she was able to remain on station with _Saratoga_, cruising at a speed of 25 knots (46 km/h; 29 mph). The other two ships were not so lucky, with _Wasp_ being [scuttled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuttling "Scuttling") that evening and _O'Brien_ eventually foundering a month later when her hull finally buckled from the damage.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank248%E2%80%93250-22)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer194%E2%80%93195-23)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHornfischer133%E2%80%93134-24) After withdrawing from the area, _North Carolina_ was detached to [Pearl Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_Harbor "Pearl Harbor") to make repairs, which lasted from 30 September to 17 November.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985277-25)

After returning to the South Pacific, _North Carolina_ resumed screening _Saratoga_ and _Enterprise_, which had also completed repairs by this time. The American fleet had been strengthened by _North Carolina_'s [sister ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_ship "Sister ship")[_Washington_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Washington_(BB-56) "USS Washington (BB-56)"), which served as the [flagship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagship "Flagship") of Rear Admiral [Willis Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willis_Lee "Willis Lee").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank503-26) The two battleships were grouped together as TF 64 under Lee's command.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHornfischer383-27) The ships covered convoys carrying soldiers and supplies to the [Solomon Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solomon_Islands "Solomon Islands") for the rest of 1942 and into 1943 as the Guadalcanal campaign ground on.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) These operations included covering a group of seven transports carrying elements of the [25th Infantry Division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/25th_Infantry_Division_(United_States) "25th Infantry Division (United States)") to Guadalcanal from 1 to 4 January 1943. During another of these convoy operations later that month, the battleships, which by this time had been reinforced by the battleship [_Indiana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Indiana_(BB-58) "USS Indiana (BB-58)"), were too far south to be able to reach the American cruiser force during the [Battle of Rennell Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Rennell_Island "Battle of Rennell Island") at the end of the month.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer224-28)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFrank548-29)

_North Carolina_ returned to Pearl Harbor in March for a refit that lasted for more than a month and included the installation of radars and improved fire control equipment.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) On returning to the South Pacific, she joined the battleship group of TF 36, now commanded by Rear Admiral [Glenn B. Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_B._Davis "Glenn B. Davis") and consisting of _Indiana_ and [_Massachusetts_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Massachusetts_(BB-59) "USS Massachusetts (BB-59)"). The battleship and carrier groups covered amphibious assault forces during [Operation Cartwheel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Cartwheel "Operation Cartwheel"), the campaign to isolate the Japanese stronghold at [Rabaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabaul "Rabaul"), in late June and early July. They did not see action during the campaign, as fighting was limited to both sides' light forces.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer258-30) In September, she made another trip to Pearl Harbor to make preparations for the attack on the [Gilbert Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_Islands "Gilbert Islands").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)

### Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign")]

Main article: [Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_and_Marshall_Islands_campaign "Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_underway_in_the_Gilbert_islands%2C_November_1943.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_underway_in_the_Gilbert_islands%2C_November_1943.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)_underway_in_the_Gilbert_islands,_November_1943.jpg)

_North Carolina_ underway during the Gilberts campaign

For the assault on the Gilberts, the fleet was organized into TF 50, which was divided into several task groups (TG). The ship sortied on 10 November, once again in company with _Enterprise_ as part of TG 50.2 to support the [Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilbert_and_Marshall_Islands_campaign "Gilbert and Marshall Islands campaign"), which began with assaults on [Makin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makin_(islands) "Makin (islands)"), [Tarawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarawa "Tarawa"), and [Abemama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abemama "Abemama"). The group also included _Massachusetts_ and _Indiana_ and a pair of light carriers and six destroyers. _North Carolina_ covered the carriers while they raided the islands beginning on 19 November. On 8 December, _North Carolina_ was detached to form TG 50.8 with the other battleships of the fleet—_Massachusetts_, _Indiana_, _South Dakota_, and _Washington_—again under Lee's command. The ships bombarded the island of [Nauru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nauru "Nauru") while the fleet prepared for the next operation in the campaign in the [Marshalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marshall_Islands "Marshall Islands"). _North Carolina_ then escorted the carrier [_Bunker Hill_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Bunker_Hill_(CV-17) "USS Bunker Hill (CV-17)") during a series of strikes on [Kavieng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kavieng "Kavieng") on the island of [New Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Ireland_(island) "New Ireland (island)") in late December.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer289,_292-31)

On 6 January 1944, TF 58, the [fast carrier task force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fast_carrier_task_force "Fast carrier task force"), was created under the command of Rear Admiral [Marc Mitscher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Mitscher "Marc Mitscher"); _North Carolina_ continued in her role as an escort for the fleet's carriers with the unit as part of TG 58.2. During the [Battle of Kwajalein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Kwajalein "Battle of Kwajalein"), _North Carolina_ initially remained with the carriers during the pre-invasion bombardment, but was then detached to close with the island and join the bombardment group targeting [Roi-Namur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roi-Namur "Roi-Namur"), which also included _Washington_, _Indiana_, and _Massachusetts_. During the attack, she sank a [cargo ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cargo_ship "Cargo ship") in the harbor. After the islands were conquered in four days of heavy fighting, TF 58 departed to raid [Truk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuuk_Lagoon "Chuuk Lagoon"), which had been Japan's primary staging area in the central Pacific. By this time, _North Carolina_ had been transferred to TG 58.3. The attack, codenamed [Operation Hailstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Hailstone "Operation Hailstone"), inflicted serious damage, sinking or destroying 39 ships, destroying 211 aircraft and damaging another 104 planes.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer303,_306-32)

With the Marshalls and Gilberts secured, the fast carrier task force embarked on a series of raids in the central Pacific to prepare for the upcoming attack on the [Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_Islands "Mariana Islands"). The fleet sortied from [Majuro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Majuro "Majuro"), its new base in the Marshalls, in late March to begin the first attack on [Palau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palau "Palau") and [Woleai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woleai "Woleai"), conducted from 31 March to 1 April. During these operations, _North Carolina_ shot down a Japanese aircraft. The fleet then sailed south to support the US Army's [landing at Hollandia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Hollandia "Battle of Hollandia") during the [New Guinea campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Guinea_campaign "New Guinea campaign") from 13 to 24 April. Another attack on Truk followed on 29–30 April; _North Carolina_ shot down another Japanese aircraft during the attack. Two of her Kingfisher floatplanes were sent to rescue a downed pilot who had crashed off the [reef](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reef "Reef"); one of them [capsized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capsize "Capsize") on landing and the second was unable to take off with the additional weight from the first plane's crew and the pilot they had gone to pick up, so the submarine [_Tang_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Tang_(SS-306) "USS Tang (SS-306)") picked up the men instead. On 1 May, _North Carolina_ and six other battleships organized as TG 58.7 bombarded [Pohnpei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pohnpei "Pohnpei"), destroying Japanese artillery batteries, anti-aircraft guns, and damaging the airfield on the island. TF 58 then returned to its bases in Majuro and [Eniwetok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eniwetok "Eniwetok") on 4 May; from there, _North Carolina_ departed to Pearl Harbor for repairs to her [rudder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rudder "Rudder").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer318%E2%80%93319,_321-33)

### Mariana and Palau Islands campaign

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Mariana and Palau Islands campaign")]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_firing_broadside_c1944.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_firing_broadside_c1944.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)_firing_broadside_c1944.jpg)

_North Carolina_ firing a [broadside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadside_(naval) "Broadside (naval)"), c. 1944

Main article: [Mariana and Palau Islands campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_and_Palau_Islands_campaign "Mariana and Palau Islands campaign")

After completing repairs, _North Carolina_ rejoined the fleet at Majuro while it was preparing for the attack on the Marianas. On arriving, she returned to TG 58.7, which was distributed between the four carrier task groups. She and the rest of TF 58 sortied on 6 June to launch the first assault in the campaign, targeting the island of [Saipan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saipan "Saipan"). In addition to screening the carriers, _North Carolina_ also bombarded the island to cover the [minesweepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minesweeper "Minesweeper") as they cleared paths to the invasion beach. She shelled [Tanapag Harbor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tanapag_Harbor "Tanapag Harbor"), sank several small vessels, and destroyed several supply dumps. On 15 June, the [marines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USMC "USMC") went ashore and a Japanese counterattack struck the fleet, though all but two of the aircraft were shot down by the carriers' [combat air patrol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Combat_air_patrol "Combat air patrol"); of those two, _North Carolina_ shot one down. The landing was a breach of Japan's inner defensive perimeter that triggered the Japanese fleet to launch a major counter-thrust with the [1st Mobile Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Mobile_Fleet_(Imperial_Japanese_Navy) "1st Mobile Fleet (Imperial Japanese Navy)"), the main carrier strike force.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer335-34)

As the Japanese fleet approached, _North Carolina_ and the rest of TF 58 steamed to meet it on 18 June, leading to the [Battle of the Philippine Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_the_Philippine_Sea "Battle of the Philippine Sea") on 19–20 June. _North Carolina_ and the other battleships, with four cruisers and thirteen destroyers, were deployed some 15 nautical miles (28 km; 17 mi) west of the carrier groups to screen the likely path of approach. The Japanese launched their aircraft first, and as they probed the American fleet's defenses, _North Carolina_ and _Washington_ were the first battleships to open fire on the attacking Japanese aircraft. During the action, which was fought primarily by the carriers, the US fleet inflicted serious losses on the Japanese, destroying hundreds of their aircraft and sinking three carriers. In the course of the battle, _North Carolina_ shot down two Japanese aircraft. _North Carolina_ remained on station off the Marianas for the next two weeks before being detached for an overhaul at the [Puget Sound Navy Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puget_Sound_Navy_Yard "Puget Sound Navy Yard").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEY'Blood68,_79-35)

### Later operations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Later operations")]

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_in_heavy_seas%2C_December_1944.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_in_heavy_seas%2C_December_1944.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)_in_heavy_seas,_December_1944.jpg)

_North Carolina_ in heavy seas in December 1944

Repairs lasted through October, keeping _North Carolina_ from participating in much of the [Philippines campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines_campaign_(1944%E2%80%931945) "Philippines campaign (1944–1945)"), and she rejoined the fleet at its new forward base at [Ulithi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulithi "Ulithi") on 7 November. There, she joined TG 38.3, the fast carrier task force having passed from [Fifth Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Fifth_Fleet "United States Fifth Fleet") to [Third Fleet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Third_Fleet "United States Third Fleet") command and accordingly being renumbered from 50-series to 30-series designations. The carriers then embarked on a series of strikes on Japanese positions on [Leyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyte "Leyte"), [Luzon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luzon "Luzon"), and the [Visayas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visayas "Visayas") to support Army operations ashore. During these operations, _North Carolina_ shot down a [kamikaze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamikaze "Kamikaze") suicide aircraft. The attacks continued into mid-December and intensified during the [invasion of Mindoro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Mindoro "Battle of Mindoro") on 15 December. Three days later, the fleet was cruising off the Philippines when it was hit by [Typhoon Cobra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Cobra "Typhoon Cobra"). _North Carolina_ was not seriously damaged, but three destroyers were sunk in the storm.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer377-36)

After returning to Ulithi, the fast carrier task force began a series of strikes on targets on [Formosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formosa "Formosa"), the coast of [French Indochina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_Indochina "French Indochina"), occupied China, and the [Ryukyu Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryukyu_Islands "Ryukyu Islands") in January 1945. _North Carolina_ remained in TG 38.3 for the operation, and her carrier group struck northern Formosa on 3–4 January, but poor weather hampered flight operations. Further attacks struck targets on Luzon on 6 and 7 January to destroy reserves of kamikazes there. On 10 January, the carrier groups entered the [South China Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_China_Sea "South China Sea") to strike targets in French Indochina on the assumption that significant Japanese naval forces were present, but only merchant ships and a number of minor warships were caught and sunk there. During these raids, other elements of the Allied fleet [invaded Lingayen Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invasion_of_Lingayen_Gulf "Invasion of Lingayen Gulf") on Luzon.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer380,_383-37)

In February, she escorted carriers during attacks on the Japanese island of [Honshu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honshu "Honshu") to disrupt Japanese air forces that might interfere with the planned [invasion of Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Iwo_Jima "Battle of Iwo Jima") in the [Bonin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonin_Islands "Bonin Islands"). Fifth Fleet had re-assumed command of the fast carrier task force by this point, and _North Carolina_ was now part of TG 58.4. The fleet sortied from Ulithi on 10 February, and after conducting training exercises off [Tinian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tinian "Tinian") on the 12th, refueled at sea on 14 February and continued on north to launch strikes on the Tokyo area two days later. The raids continued through 17 February and the next day, the fleet withdrew to refuel and TG 58.4 was sent to hit other islands in the Bonin chain to further isolate [Iwo Jima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iwo_Jima "Iwo Jima"). During the preparatory bombardment for that attack, _North Carolina_, _Washington_, and the heavy cruiser [_Indianapolis_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Indianapolis_(CA-35) "USS Indianapolis (CA-35)") were detached from the task group to reinforce TF 54, the assault force for the invasion; she remained on station during the marine assault and provided fire support as they fought their way across the island through 22 February. The next day, the carrier groups reassembled and refueled on 24 February for further operations against the Japanese mainland.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer393%E2%80%93394-38)

After leaving Iwo Jima, the fleet resumed air attacks on the [Home Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_Archipelago "Japanese Archipelago") to prepare for the next amphibious assault on [Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okinawa_Island "Okinawa Island") in the Ryukyus. The first of these, on 25 and 26 February, hit targets in the Tokyo area, followed by another attack on Iwo Jima the next day. The fleet refueled on 28 February and on 1 March raided Okinawa, thereafter returning to Ulithi on 4 March.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer393-39) While in Ulithi, the fleet was reorganized and _North Carolina_ was transferred to TG 58.3. The fleet sortied on 14 March for additional attacks on Japan; the ships refueled on 16 March on the way and they launched their aircraft two days later to hit targets on [Kyushu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyushu "Kyushu"). The attacks continued into the next day, causing significant damage to Japanese facilities on the island and sinking or damaging numerous warships. The task groups withdrew to refuel and reorganize on 22 March, as several carriers had been damaged by kamikaze and air attacks. The carriers [_Wasp_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Wasp_(CV-18) "USS Wasp (CV-18)") and [_Franklin_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Franklin_(CV-13) "USS Franklin (CV-13)") were badly damaged by bombs, and _North Carolina_ was assigned to the group of ships tasked with escorting them back to Ulithi for repairs.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer399%E2%80%93400-40)

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_underway_at_sea_on_3_June_1946_%28NH_97267%29.jpg/250px-USS_North_Carolina_%28BB-55%29_underway_at_sea_on_3_June_1946_%28NH_97267%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)_underway_at_sea_on_3_June_1946_(NH_97267).jpg)

_North Carolina_ off New York in June 1946

Carrier raids on the Home Islands and the Ryukyus continued after the [landing on Okinawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Okinawa "Battle of Okinawa") on 1 April. When _North Carolina_ returned to the fleet, she was assigned to TG 58.2. Five days later, _North Carolina_ shot down three kamikazes. In the furious anti-aircraft [barrage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrage_(artillery) "Barrage (artillery)"), another ship accidentally hit _North Carolina_ with a 5-inch shell, killing three and wounding forty-four. On 7 April, the Japanese launched a major air–naval counterattack on the landing centered on the battleship [_Yamato_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_battleship_Yamato "Japanese battleship Yamato"), which was largely defeated by the carriers, though _North Carolina_ shot down one Japanese bomber. Another major kamikaze attack struck the fleet on 11 April. She shot down two more on 17 April, and two days later she was sent to support infantry attacks on Okinawa before departing for another overhaul at Pearl Harbor.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer407%E2%80%93408,_410-41)

_North Carolina_ returned to the fleet in [Leyte Gulf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leyte_Gulf "Leyte Gulf") in late June before it embarked on another series of attacks on Japan on 1 July. By this time, the fast carrier task force had been transferred to Third Fleet, so the battleship joined TG 38.3. The air attacks began on 10 July, with over a thousand aircraft hitting airfields around Tokyo. The strikes continued for more than a week, until a typhoon approached and forced the fleet to withdraw to avoid it on 19 July. During these operations, one of her Kingfishers picked up a downed pilot in [Tokyo Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tokyo_Bay "Tokyo Bay") under heavy fire. Following the [Japanese surrender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrender_of_Japan "Surrender of Japan") on 15 August, _North Carolina_ contributed men for the initial [occupation force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occupation_of_Japan "Occupation of Japan") and entered [Sagami Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagami_Bay "Sagami Bay") on 27 August with the rest of the fleet. She thereafter patrolled the coast until 5 September, when she steamed into Tokyo Bay to reembark the men. The next day, she was assigned to TF 11 along with the three [_New Mexico_-class battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Mexico-class_battleship "New Mexico-class battleship"), a pair of light carriers, and a squadron of destroyers to return to the United States. From there, she sailed south to Okinawa to take on men bound for home as part of [Operation Magic Carpet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operation_Magic_Carpet "Operation Magic Carpet").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERohwer421%E2%80%93422,_428%E2%80%93429,_431-42) The ship suffered a total of 10 crew dead and 67 wounded during her wartime service.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESneed85-43) The ship received 15 [battle stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_star "Battle star") during her wartime service, the most of any battleship in the US fleet and placing her among the [most decorated US Naval vessels of World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Most_decorated_US_Naval_vessels_of_World_War_II "Most decorated US Naval vessels of World War II").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-44)

She transited the Panama Canal on 8 October and arrived in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") on 17 October. Subsequently she underwent an overhaul in the [Brooklyn Navy Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Navy_Yard "Brooklyn Navy Yard") and thereafter conducted training operations off the east coast, including a training cruise for [midshipmen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midshipmen "Midshipmen") from the [US Naval Academy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Naval_Academy "US Naval Academy") in the Caribbean in mid-1946.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9)_North Carolina_ was the only American [treaty battleship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_battleship "Treaty battleship") to see any significant service after the end of the war.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_198097-3)

### Decommissioning

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Decommissioning")]

The ship was decommissioned on 27 June 1947 in New York and placed in reserve.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) While she was out of service, the Navy considered several plans to modernize or convert the ship for other purposes. The first series of studies in 1954 revolved around improving the ship's speed to 31 knots (57 km/h; 36 mph), which would require a significant reduction in displacement and a much more powerful propulsion system. The displacement issue could be solved by the removal of the rear turret, but there was not enough room in the hull to place a power plant necessary to reach the desired speed. The Navy also evaluated a proposal to convert _North Carolina_ into a [helicopter carrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter_carrier "Helicopter carrier"); the plan would have involved removing all of her main and secondary guns (though the forward turret would be retained to keep the ship balanced properly) in exchange for a flight deck and facilities for twenty-eight [helicopters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicopter "Helicopter") and a battery of sixteen 3-inch (76 mm) guns. The Navy ultimately decided that a new, purpose-built helicopter carrier would be cheaper and so the project was abandoned.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFriedman_1985397%E2%80%93401-45)

She remained in the Navy's inventory until she was stricken from the [Naval Vessel Register](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naval_Vessel_Register "Naval Vessel Register") on 1 June 1960, slated to be [broken up](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_breaking "Ship breaking") for [scrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scrap "Scrap").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) A North Carolina man, James Craig, founded a campaign to save the vessel modeled on the Battleship _Texas_ Commission that had successfully acquired the old battleship [_Texas_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Texas_(BB-35) "USS Texas (BB-35)") for preservation as a [museum ship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_ship "Museum ship"). He convinced Governor [Luther H. Hodges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luther_H._Hodges "Luther H. Hodges") to ask the Navy to delay the scrapping of the ship, and then led a campaign to raise the $250,000 necessary to prepare a site to host the vessel, to tow her there, and work to prepare her for visitors. With the help of the [WRAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WRAL-TV "WRAL-TV") TV station—which broadcast a "Save Our Ship" advertisement campaign—and numerous state newspapers, Craig was able to secure more than $330,000 for the project. Next were considerations of the site to be used; three cities were considered: [Southport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southport,_North_Carolina "Southport, North Carolina"), [Morehead City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morehead_City "Morehead City"), and [Wilmington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmington,_North_Carolina "Wilmington, North Carolina"). The latter was selected, since it was further inland and thus more protected from hurricanes.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESneed84,_87%E2%80%9388-46)

_North Carolina_ being towed to Wilmington in 1961

On 6 September 1961, _North Carolina_ was transferred to the state.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) The ship was towed out of [Bayonne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayonne,_New_Jersey "Bayonne, New Jersey"), New Jersey, bound for Wilmington, by a group of nine [tugboats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tugboat "Tugboat") on 25 September.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTESneed90-48) At one point during the trip, on 2 October, the tugs lost control of the ship in the [Cape Fear River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Fear_River "Cape Fear River") and she collided with a floating seafood restaurant, though surprisingly causing only minor damage.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-49) After her berth – located across the Cape Fear River from downtown Wilmington, about 28 miles (45 km) from the river's confluence with the Atlantic Ocean[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50) — was completed and repairs to the ship effected, she was formally opened on 29 April 1962[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDANFS-9) as a memorial to more than 11,000 North Carolinians who died while serving in the [United States armed forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_armed_forces "United States armed forces") during World War II.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50)

In 1964, a Kingfisher that had crashed in [British Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Columbia "British Columbia"), Canada, during the war and then subsequently been salvaged was donated to the museum.

In the early 1980s, when the Navy reactivated the four [_Iowa_-class battleships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iowa-class_battleship "Iowa-class battleship"), parts were cannibalized from _North Carolina_ and the other preserved battleships, including _Alabama_ and _Massachusetts_, to restore the _Iowa_ s to service. Engine room components that were no longer available in the Navy's inventory accounted for most of the material removed from the ships.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-PCH-51) The battleship was declared a [National Historic Landmark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Historic_Landmark "National Historic Landmark") on 10 November 1982; the application noted that the ship was in almost excellent condition and remained in its wartime configuration.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEButowsky-52)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERobertson-53)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTENational_Register_Digital_Assets-54)

Work to maintain the ship and improve the facility is an on-going effort. In 1998, the museum's operators ran Operation Ship Shape, a donation drive to secure funds to make repairs to the vessel, including the ship's [teak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teak "Teak") deck, which was replaced with teak from [Myanmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myanmar "Myanmar"). Funds from the campaign were also allocated to repair the ship's hull, which by the early 2000s had deteriorated significantly; in some places, corrosion had reduced the thickness of the hull plating from its original 0.625-to-0.75-inch (15.9 to 19.1 mm) thickness to as thin as 0.15 inches (3.8 mm). After considering moving the ship to a drydock for the work, which would have been prohibitively expensive, the ship's caretakers decided to use the same method used to refurbish the battleship [_Alabama_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_Alabama_(BB-60) "USS Alabama (BB-60)"): erect a [cofferdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cofferdam "Cofferdam") around the hull and pump it dry. In addition to replacing damaged hull plates, the hull also received a new coat of paint to better protect it from the elements. In 2018, a walkway was erected around the ship to allow visitors to view the ship from all sides, with funding provided by the [SECU Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Employees_Credit_Union#SECU_Foundation "State Employees Credit Union"). The walkway sits  atop the cofferdam necessary for the ship's repairs.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTERobertson-53)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHotz-55)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBuckland-56) Repairs to the ship's hull were completed in 2021.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-57)

As of the beginning of 2024, the memorial and museum is one of North Carolina's most-visited tourist sites.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50) In 2022, the museum had nearly 250,000 visitors and enjoyed the most financially successful year in its history.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50)

During the early 21st century, flooding due to a [climate change](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_change "Climate change")-related rise in sea level became an increasing problem at the museum site. A [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration")[tidal gauge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tidal_gauge "Tidal gauge") 0.5-mile (0.8 km) from the museum recorded a 9-inch (23 cm) rise in sea level between its installation in 1935 and 2023, and the museum's leaders documented a 7,000 percent increase in flooding incidents between 1961 and 2023, with 20 flooding incidents at the site during 2011. After 2013, flooding problems accelerated dramatically: In 2020, the site experienced flooding during about half of the year, and flooding continued to accelerate after that, with 200 days of flooding during 2022. By the beginning of 2024, waters from the Cape Fear River routinely overtopped [seawalls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seawall "Seawall"), flooding hundreds of spaces in the museum's parking lot as well as sidewalks and grassy areas, killing [oak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak "Oak") trees on the property, and occasionally forcing the museum to close when its only access road became submerged.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50)

To increase drainage, improve both water quality, and enhance safety of visitors, the museum's leaders decided to embark on a [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar")4.1 million construction project – expected to last from January to September 2024 – which would allow the museum to accommodate the changing landscape rather than attempt to prevent the intrusion of water. Plans called for the removal of about 800 feet (244 m) of concrete and rock barriers and their replacement with a "living shoreline" of earthen berms and native vegetation that would reduce erosion and attract a variety of animals including [shrimp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shrimp "Shrimp") and [blue crabs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_crab "Blue crab"); the removal of several acres of the parking lot prone to flooding and restoring the tidal creek and [wetland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wetland "Wetland") that existed there before 1961, to hold back water and redirect it into the river; raising the remaining portion of the parking lot above the high tide level; and planting 100 trees and shrubs in the parking lot and 130,000 native marsh plants to filter storm water runoff and create a habitat for migratory and nesting birds. The project will be funded with nearly US$2 million from [United States Government](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Government "United States Government") and North Carolina state grants, more than US$1 million from the North Carolina state budget, and funding from the [North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Carolina_Department_of_Natural_and_Cultural_Resources "North Carolina Department of Natural and Cultural Resources").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50)

With sea level rise at the site expected to increase by about 1 foot (0.3 m) between 2024 and 2050, the 2024 construction project is expected to address drainage problems until sometime between 2039 and 2044, when additional measures may become necessary to address flooding. The 2024 project is designed to accommodate additional changes that probably will be required in the mid-21st century.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USS_North_Carolina_(BB-55)#cite_note-brady20240101-50)
